nuance.situation: 꾸준히 연습하면 결국 실력이 는다고 격려하려고 해요. (You encourage someone: keep practicing and you'll improve.)

options.text: 꾸준히 연습하면 실력은 늘기 마련이야.
options.why: -기 마련이다 states a natural result, good or bad, and suits encouragement.

options.text: 꾸준히 연습하면 실력이 늘기 십상이야.
options.why: -기 십상이다 is used almost exclusively for likely unwanted outcomes; attached to a good result like improving, it sounds off, even sarcastic.

options.text: 꾸준히 연습하면 실력이 늘 지경이야.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ 지경이다 describes being pushed to an extreme (usually bad) state, not a natural payoff.

nuance.situation: 친구가 저녁을 굶으면서 무리하게 다이어트를 하고 있어요. 그러다 요요가 올 거라고 경고하려면? (A friend is crash-dieting by skipping dinner. You warn them they'll likely bounce back.)

options.text: 그렇게 굶다가는 요요가 오기 십상이야.
options.why: -다가는 … -기 십상이다 is the classic warning frame for a likely bad outcome.

options.text: 그렇게 굶다가는 요요가 온 셈이야.
options.why: -(으)ㄴ 셈이다 reckons from facts already in; it can't warn about what is likely to happen.

options.text: 그렇게 굶다가는 요요가 온 탓이야.
options.why: -(으)ㄴ 탓이다 blames a past cause for a result that has already happened, which clashes with the warning frame -다가는.

mnemonic: Picture someone glancing over their shoulder mid-action: 누가 볼세라, lest anyone see.
nuance: Gives the anxious motive behind a precaution: the main clause is what someone does so that the feared thing won't happen (누가 볼세라 얼른 숨겼다). Literary in flavor, but alive in a handful of set uses: 누가 볼세라, 놓칠세라, and especially 뒤질세라 / 질세라 ('not to be outdone'). The everyday equivalent is -(으)ㄹ까 봐.

contrasts.note: -기 십상이다 says a bad outcome is likely; -(으)ㄹ세라 describes acting to head it off.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마 손을 놓칠세라 꼭 붙잡고 걸었다.
examples.en: The child walked clutching his mother's hand, afraid of losing hold of it.

examples.ko: 한 업체가 가격을 내리자 경쟁사들도 질세라 할인 행사를 시작했다.
examples.en: When one company cut prices, its rivals, not to be outdone, launched sales of their own.

cloze.sentence: 그는 누가 {{}} 편지를 서둘러 서랍에 넣었다.
cloze.en: He hurried the letter into the drawer, lest anyone see it.

nearMiss.hint: Same idea and more everyday; the cue asks for the literary -(으)ㄹ세라.

cloze.sentence: 아이가 {{}} 엄마는 발소리를 죽이며 방을 나왔다.
cloze.en: Careful not to wake the child, the mother crept out of the room.

nearMiss.hint: Same idea and more everyday; the cue asks for the literary -(으)ㄹ세라.

cloze.sentence: 옆 사람이 {{}} 그녀는 수화기를 손으로 가리고 속삭였다.
cloze.en: Afraid the person next to her might overhear, she cupped the receiver and whispered.

nearMiss.hint: 듣다 is ㄷ-irregular: 들을세라.

cloze.sentence: 할머니는 손주가 {{}} 이불을 몇 번이나 덮어 주셨다.
cloze.en: For fear her grandchild would get cold, Grandma tucked the blanket in again and again.

nearMiss.hint: 춥다 is ㅂ-irregular: 추울세라.

cloze.sentence: 형이 노래를 한 곡 뽑자 동생도 {{}} 마이크를 잡았다.
cloze.en: When the older brother belted out a song, the younger one, not to be outdone, grabbed the mic.

cloze.sentence: 버스를 {{}} 정류장까지 숨이 차게 뛰었다.
cloze.en: Afraid of missing the bus, I ran to the stop until I was out of breath.

cloze.sentence: 그는 국이 {{}} 쟁반을 조심조심 들고 왔다.
cloze.en: He carried the tray in gingerly, lest the soup slop over.

cloze.sentence: 커피가 {{}} 얼른 들고 회의실로 갔다.
cloze.en: Before the coffee could cool, I hurried it into the meeting room.

nearMiss.hint: Same idea and more everyday; the cue asks for -(으)ㄹ세라.

cloze.sentence: 시민들은 좋은 자리를 {{}} 새벽부터 줄을 섰다.
cloze.en: Afraid of losing a good spot, people lined up from dawn.

nuance.situation: 한 회사가 신제품을 내자 경쟁사도 뒤처지지 않으려고 곧바로 비슷한 제품을 냈어요. 기사 문장으로 쓰려면? (One firm launched a product, and its rival, not to be outdone, followed at once.)

options.text: 경쟁사도 이에 뒤질세라 비슷한 제품을 내놓았다.
options.why: 뒤질세라 is the set use: acting so as not to fall behind.

options.text: 경쟁사도 이에 뒤지기 십상이라 비슷한 제품을 내놓았다.
options.why: -기 십상이다 predicts that falling behind is likely; it doesn't express the motive of not being outdone, and the sentence turns muddled.

options.text: 경쟁사도 이에 뒤지는 바람에 비슷한 제품을 내놓았다.
options.why: -는 바람에 reports an unwanted cause that already happened: it says the rival did fall behind, the opposite of the point.

nuance.situation: 시험에 떨어질까 봐 걱정돼서 밤낮없이 공부했어요. 이 사정을 글로 쓰려면? (Worried you might fail the exam, you studied day and night. You write about it.)

options.text: 시험에 떨어질세라 밤낮없이 공부했다.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ세라 gives the feared outcome behind the precaution: failing.

options.text: 시험에 붙을세라 밤낮없이 공부했다.
options.why: -(으)ㄹ세라 marks the outcome you fear. Passing is what you want, so this says you studied for fear of passing.

options.text: 시험에 떨어지는 바람에 밤낮없이 공부했다.
options.why: -는 바람에 says the failure actually happened and caused the studying, which isn't the story.
